How things change through exposure to other factors, designing for feedback loops where systems & people mutually shape each other.

Interconnectivity

Revealing how meaning emerges from relationships between ideas, people, & technologies rather than from isolated elements.

Perception

Designing with awareness that we actively construct reality from sensory input, shaped by attention, memory, language, & what we're primed to notice.

This portfolio is more than a showcase—it's a visual argument for how I think about design, technology, and human experience. As someone who studied both the science of mind and the art of interaction, I believe the best solutions emerge when we understand how people think, not just what they need.

The force-directed graph you see below isn't just a creative flourish. It's a deliberate reflection of my three core themes—interconnectivity, interaction, and perception—working together. Each node represents a skill, project, or research theme, and the connections between them show how my work is truly interdisciplinary. Just like how memory works through associative networks in the brain, this portfolio lets you explore knowledge through relationships rather than rigid hierarchies.

Every design choice—from the CMYK-inspired color palette to the carefully selected typography—is intentional and grounded in principles of accessibility and cognitive science. Churn/Score Dashboard

Proactive retention through predictive analytics
Interaction
Sole Product Designer
Oct – Nov 2025
Figma
Claude AI
HTML/CSS

Background

Worthix needed a dashboard to help Customer Success teams identify at-risk accounts before they churn, moving from reactive support to proactive retention strategy.

The Problem

Customer Success teams lacked:
Early warning signals:
No visibility into at-risk accounts until too late.
Prioritization framework:
All accounts treated equally despite varying churn risk & revenue impact.
Actionable guidance:
No clear interventions when risks were identified.

Design Solution

Risk-Based Architecture

Critical Metrics First
(e.g., total expected loss) provide companies with an immediate health check
Risk Segmentation
(AKA grouping accounts by churn probability & highlighting revenue impact) makes prioritization clear
AI Churn Assistant
provides proactive analysis in a clear, accessible, and user-friendly manner

Outcome

Designs were delivered to product team and the AI assistant feature generated particular interest as a market differentiator.

Custom 3D Printed Press-On Nails

Solving fit problems through personalized fabrication
Perception
Designer & Fabricator
Jan – May 2025
3D Scanner
Blender
3D Printer
PLA
Traditional Media: gel nail polish, solid builder gel, nail e-file

The Problem

Generic press-on nails assume a standardized nail shape that doesn't take individual variation into consideration, resulting in poor fit, discomfort, & nails that pop off easily.

The Process

1.
Digital Capture
3D scanned my fingers to capture exact nail geometry & surrounding skin contours.
2.
Modeling & Refinement
Used Blender to clean up scans, isolate nail beds, & create custom-fit base shapes.
3.
Iterative Prototyping
printed multiple test versions, refining curvature, thickness, & adhesion surface area.
4.
Hand Finishing
Added handpainted embellishments to final pieces, combining the modern digital with the traditional analog.

Outcome

Successfully created custom-fit press-on nails that addressed the core fit problem of mass-produced alternatives. This project demonstrates end-to-end physical product development: identifying a real user need, prototyping through digital fabrication, & finishing with traditional techniques.

Competitive Analysis Dashboard

Designing actionable insights under startup constraints
Interconnectivity
Sole Product Designer
Oct 2025
Figma
Claude AI
Cursor AI
GitHub
HTML/CSS

Background

Worthix Hub is an AI-powered platform that scrapes and analyzes online reviews to help companies understand customer sentiment. The platform generates "Keep Doing" and "Do Better" summaries, but clients struggled to act on these insights without visual comparison tools.

The challenge:

Clients requested in-app data visualization capabilities to benchmark against competitors and industry trends, rather than exporting data to external tools like PowerBI.

The Problem

The initial prototype provided delivered insights but lacked:
Visual comparison:
Clients couldn't see performance relative to competitors or industry averages.
Good information hierarchy:
All data treated equally, making it difficult to identify priorities.
Varied actionability:
Received analysis without clear next steps.

Design Solution

Information Architecture: Context Before Detail

I structured the dashboard to mirror how analysts approach competitive positioning:
Industry Trends First
separated by topic, establishing baseline performance expectations.
Topic Clustering
reveals how themes distribute across companies, making competitive positioning visible at a glance.
AI-Generated Insights
strengths, weaknesses, and recommended next steps, keeping the customer from questioning what comes next.

Outcome

Designs delivered to product team within the 3-day timeline for phased implementation. This project reinforced the importance of balancing user needs with technical feasibility, making strategic decisions with limited information, & designing systems that scale beyond initial requirements.

Hi! I'm Lara

I'm a recent graduate from Wellesley College with a unique perspective shaped by two complementary fields: understanding how humans think and creating the technologies they interact with.

My approach is rooted in a simple belief: nothing exists in isolation. Everything—systems, people, ideas—is in constant conversation. This is why I'm drawn to the intersection of cognitive science and interactive media, focusing on how we interact with systems, how systems interconnect, and how we perceive information.

I'm also deeply influenced by the weak Sapir-Whorf hypothesis: language shapes thought. The way we present information—through interfaces, visualizations, or interactions—fundamentally affects how people understand it. Most things aren't inherently complicated; they become complicated when we present them poorly. That's why design, UX, and presentation matter.

My work combines research-backed insights from cognitive psychology with technical execution, creating experiences that don't just function—they communicate clearly and adapt to how humans actually think.
